goal: Analyze the competitive landscape of NVIDIA in the AI accelerator market

report.executive_summary: NVIDIA holds a dominant position in the AI accelerator market with an 86% market share, but faces growing competition from custom ASICs and companies like AMD, Broadcom, and Marvell.

competitors.name: AMD
competitors.summary: AMD's Instinct series is gaining traction in data center inference deployments.

competitors.name: Broadcom
competitors.summary: Broadcom is gaining ground in custom AI accelerators (ASICs).

competitors.name: Marvell
competitors.summary: Marvell is gaining ground in custom AI accelerators (ASICs).

competitors.name: Groq
competitors.summary: Groq's LPX inference accelerator is being integrated with NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform for higher throughput.

recent_developments.text: NVIDIA launched the Vera Rubin platform, a six-chip system later expanded to seven chips, including the Groq 3 LPU.
NVIDIA announced the BlueField-4 STX Storage Architecture and the Vera CPU, purpose-built for agentic AI.

market_signals.text: The AI accelerators market is expected to grow at a 24.29% CAGR from 2026 to 2031.
Cloud/data-center deployments captured 75% of the AI accelerators market share in 2024.

risks.text: NVIDIA's market share may decrease to the 70-80% range by 2028 as custom ASICs and AMD's Instinct series gain traction.
NVIDIA's reliance on TSMC for chip fabrication could pose supply chain risks.
